curriculumDefinition.commandsAndConcepts: `iw aw iW aW`; `i" a"`, `i' a'`, ``i` a` ``; `i( a(`, `i) a)`, `ib ab`; `i[ a[`, `i] a]`; `i{ a{`, `i} a}`, `iB aB`; `i< a<`, `i> a>`; `is as`, `ip ap`, `it at`
curriculumDefinition.learningOutcome: Choose inside versus around and apply any learned operator to a structural object
curriculumDefinition.representativeExercises: Change a quoted value; delete function arguments; yank an object literal; uppercase a word; indent a paragraph; replace tag contents
curriculumDefinition.priorityAndPortability: Core. Tag and angle-bracket objects are exercised only where the buffer makes their boundaries unambiguous

lessons.title: Choose contents or surroundings
lessons.objective: Use inside and around word objects with previously learned operators.

activities.body: A text object selects a complete item around the cursor, such as a word or quoted text. Use `i` for only the contents, or `a` to include the surrounding quotes, brackets, or nearby space.
activities.contrast: A motion travels somewhere; a text object describes what to act on.

activities.title: Structures are reusable ranges
activities.body: You can now apply familiar operators to words, quotes, balanced delimiters, prose blocks, and HTML elements.
takeaways: Choose inside when boundaries should remain.
Choose around when delimiters or separator whitespace belong to the edit.
Compose operators with objects instead of counting characters.

reference.purpose: Target word or WORD contents and surroundings.
Target quote contents or include quotes and adjacent whitespace.
notes: Quote objects remain on one line.

i{ / a{ / i} / a} / iB / aB

notes: Use tag objects for HTML elements.
